title: Planet formation in intermediate-separation binary systems
question: Characterise the individual circum-primary and circum-secondary discs in the intermediate-separation binary systems KK Oph and HD 144668 to understand how binarity impacts disc evolution and planet-forming potential.

data.arrays: 12 m array (41 antennas for KK Oph, 38 antennas for HD 144668)
data.sensitivity: Band 6 continuum rms: 0.18 mJy/beam (HD 144668), 0.16 mJy/beam (KK Oph); Band 7 continuum rms: 0.53 mJy/beam (HD 144668)

what.value: Rest frequencies of 13CO and C18O J=2-1 from the LAMDA database

evidence.quote: The spectral setup included $^{13}$CO and C$^{18}$O J$=$2–1 lines with rest frequencies of 220.3986841281 and 219.5603541 respectively (LAMDA database, https://home.strw.leidenuniv.nl/ moldata/CO.html)

what.value: Gaia DR2 distance to KK Oph of 221.1 +12.4/-10.4 pc

evidence.quote: It is not present in the Hipparcos catalogue and Gaia DR2 assigns to it a distance of 221.1$^{+12.4}_{-10.4}$ pc (cite: 2018A&A...620A.128V), though it includes the warning label that it might be unreliable.

what.value: Dust map used to derive E(B-V) extinction values towards KK Oph and HD 144668

evidence.quote: Using the dust map of (cite: 2019A&A...625A.135L) and the Gaia DR2 distances and coordinates to the primary stars, we obtain an E(B-V)=0.046${\pm}$0.039 for KK Oph and E(B-V)=0.015$^{+0.022}_{-0.015}$ for HD 144668 system.

what.value: Millimetre fluxes at 0.88, 0.856, and 6.9 mm for the 253-1536 binary in Orion used to compute its differential opacity spectral index

evidence.loc: mm spectral index from B6/B7 for HD144668
evidence.quote: Using the same approach as for the calculation of $\Delta\beta$ for HD 144688 in Sect. [4](#results), and fluxes of the 253-1536 A and B from (cite: 2011ApJ...739L...8R) at 0.88 and 6.9 mm we obtain $\Delta\beta_{253-1536}$=0.04$^{+0.10}_{-0.05}$.

evidence.loc: mm spectral index from B6/B7 for HD144668
evidence.quote: Using the same 6.9 mm fluxes combined with newer 0.856 mm observations of (cite: 2009ApJ...699L..55M) we obtain $\Delta\beta_{253-1536}$=-0.09$^{+0.11}_{-0.09}$.

recipe.goal: Determine optical/NIR stellar positions and binary separations
recipe.method: Extract primary star coordinates and parallaxes from Gaia DR2 (verifying reliability via RUWE), and fit stellar profiles (or saturated PSF wings) on pipeline-reduced VLT/NACO 2 um adaptive optics images to measure binary separations and position angles.
key_parameters: NACO image resolution 75 mas, position precision 0.2 pixels (2.7 mas) for KK Oph
assumptions: Distances of 221 pc for KK Oph and 161.1 pc for HD 144668

recipe.goal: Fit 2D Gaussians to continuum sources and subtract point-source models to identify outer disc asymmetries
recipe.method: Fit 2D Gaussians to isolated primary and secondary continuum emission in Band 6 and Band 7 images using CASA imfit, place point sources of the fitted flux and position in blank images, convolve with the synthesized beam, and subtract from the ALMA images.
assumptions: Unresolved inner disc emission can be modelled as a point source convolved with the synthesized beam

recipe.goal: Calculate disc dust masses from 1.2 mm continuum fluxes
recipe.method: Compute dust masses from the 1.2 mm integrated continuum fluxes using the optically thin thermal dust emission equation M_dust = S_nu * D^2 / (kappa_nu * B_nu(T)).
key_parameters: T = 20 K; kappa_nu = 1.15 cm^2/g_dust (also stated as 2 cm^2/g in Sect. 4.2.3); D = 161.1 pc (HD 144668) and 221 pc (KK Oph)
assumptions: Optically thin millimetre dust emission, isothermal dust temperature of 20 K, maximum grain size around 1 mm

recipe.goal: Compute individual and differential millimetre spectral indices and grain size power-law slopes for HD 144668 A and B
recipe.method: Calculate flux spectral index alpha, opacity spectral index beta = alpha - 2, and grain size power-law index p = 3 + beta/beta_ISM from Band 6 (230 GHz) and Band 7 (345 GHz) fluxes; then compute the calibration-independent differential opacity index beta^A - beta^B = log(R) / log(nu_1/nu_2) from the flux ratios R = (S_nu1^A * S_nu2^B) / (S_nu2^A * S_nu1^B).
key_parameters: beta_ISM = 1.7; nu_1 = 230 GHz (1.3 mm), nu_2 = 345 GHz (0.87 mm); TORUS minimum grain size = 3.5 Angstrom, a_max = 1 mm and 1 cm, p = 3.2 and 3.5
assumptions: Rayleigh-Jeans regime (hv/k_B T << 1), optically thin emission arising from the same temperature layer (20 K) at both wavelengths, constant beta between nu_1 and nu_2

recipe.goal: Derive upper limits on disc gas masses and gas-to-dust ratios from 13CO non-detections
recipe.method: Integrate 13CO J=2-1 emission over 0 to 8 km/s to obtain flux upper limits, solve analytically for fractional upper-state population x_u using a Boltzmann distribution in LTE (partition function summed to J=40), compute 13CO molecular mass in the optically thin limit, and convert to total gas mass using the 13CO fractional abundance.
key_parameters: Velocity integration range: 0 to 8 km/s; T = 20 K; partition function maximum level J = 40; 13CO relative abundance = 1.3e-6
assumptions: Local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE), optically thin 13CO J=2-1 emission, gas temperature of 20 K, standard 13CO abundance of 1.3e-6

recipe.goal: Compute probability distributions of tidal truncation radii for the primary and secondary discs
recipe.method: Sample unknown binary orbital parameters (omega, e, i, M) using a Monte Carlo approach (10 million realizations into 1000 radial bins from 0 to 400 au), solve Kepler's equation by bisection for eccentric anomaly E to obtain deprojection factor F = a/a_p, and compute tidal truncation radius R_t for primary and secondary discs across the range of stellar mass ratios.
key_parameters: 1000 bins from 0 to 400 au; 10 million random orbital parameter sets; e in [0, 0.7]; omega in [0, 2pi]; M in [0, 2pi]; a_p = 1.6088'' (KK Oph, d=221 pc) and 1.46'' (HD 144668, d=161 pc); stellar mass ratios psi = 1.5-1.67 (KK Oph) and 2.2-4.285 (HD 144668)
assumptions: Elliptic Keplerian orbit with eccentricity uniformly distributed between 0 and 0.7, random orientation, and observational size limits set by the ALMA beam (primaries > 72 au for KK Oph and > 43 au for HD 144668; secondaries < 72 au and < 43 au)

score_reason: Raw data are public in ALMA/ESO/Gaia archives, calibration and imaging steps use standard CASA tasks with stated versions and robust weighting, and analytical equations for dust/gas masses, differential beta, and tidal truncation are explicitly written out. However, minor internal inconsistencies in the stated dust opacity value (1.15 vs 2 cm^2/g) and unstated spectral-cube extraction apertures slightly hinder exact numerical reproduction.
rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA data, straightforward continuum imaging and CASA imfit Gaussian fitting, and explicit analytical equations for dust masses, differential spectral index, gas mass upper limits, and Monte Carlo truncation radii.
